decisions.statement: A change reaches only a change acting on the same target type.
Which page types are changes is read from the page types the index carries.
A page type extending a change page type is a change page type too.
The code beside a change is found through the extension that change states.
An address is read from the parse rather than from the text.
A change's body spelling another change's address is taken as reaching it.
An address is judged wherever in the body that address is written.
An address handed to a helper rather than to a runner is judged the same.
An address built as the body runs is refused rather than read.
A refusal for an address built that way names the line spelling it.
Which built shape could be an address is read from the page types the index carries.
Which call an address is handed to is not read here.
An address reaching no page is let through.
A refusal names both changes, both target types, and the address.
A refusal is filed at the reaching change's page.
One change naming several addresses that reach across is refused once for each.
One address spelled twice in one body is refused once.
A change whose page the landing takes away is not judged.
The check runs where a change's code is carried and that change's page is not.
Running at change keeps a new reach across target types from landing.
Whether an address reaches a page at all is not judged here.

definition: the check refusing a change that reaches a change acting on another target type
